mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE first exceeds 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo avg for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of above-average PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting rapid earnings revisions as supply expands and bottlenecks resolve.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO growth and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
